To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CMS measurement of the W polarization is sensitive to new physics, and that the measurement can be used to constrain the new physics parameters.

(i) the CMS collaboration’s measurement of the W-boson polarisation in pp → W±+ jet → e± +jet+ is sensitive to gV, the vectorial coupling of the W-bose to the fermions, and (ii) the CMS collaboration has not yet reached a sufficient sensitivity to gV to be sensitive to deviations from the Standard-Model prediction for this coupling, but it is possible that this could be achieved in future measurements.
the CMS measurement of the polarization of the W-boson is a powerful probe for new physics at LHC.

the W-boson polarisation at the LHC is not a simple observable.

the W-boson polarisation can be used to probe the underlying theory of W-boson interactions with matter.
